scenario.summary: Storm-3119 (YAM Store) functions as an infrastructure broker that hijacks Microsoft 365 and Azure environments through automated reconnaissance and application-level credential abuse. These compromised environments and PaaS phishing kits (Storm-2990) are then used by downstream actors to conduct large-scale credential and financial theft, leveraging real-time victim interaction via WebSockets and Telegram.

hunt.name: Phishing Infrastructure and Interactive Exfiltration
hunt.description: This hunt targets the interactive phases of the Storm-2990 and Storm-3119 phishing ecosystem. It focuses on the behavioral hallmarks of the Iron Man System: high-frequency WebSocket-like traffic for real-time operator-victim interaction and exfiltration via the Telegram Bot API. The hunt first scopes to hosts running core productivity software targeted by this group, then fans out to identify connections to reported infrastructure and behavioral exfiltration patterns. An agent triages the converged evidence to distinguish legitimate application traffic from active phishing sessions.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) as connection_count, SUM(traffic_packets) as total_packets, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE dst_endpoint_port = 443 AND state_kind = 'log' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip HAVING total_packets > 500
config.description: Identify hosts with sustained, high-packet outbound traffic on port 443, characteristic of interactive phishing sessions.
config.expected_signal: High packet volume to an external IP seen on few hosts suggests a long-lived session like a WebSocket used for interactive harvesting.
